question: Explain how inventories are measured under AS 2 'Valuation of Inventories'. What is included in the cost of inventories, which costs are excluded, and which cost formulas may be used?
sources: AS 2, Valuation of Inventories (issued by ICAI)

points.label: Measurement rule
points.description: Inventories are valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
keywords: lower of cost and net realisable value

points.label: Net realisable value
points.description: Net realisable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less the estimated costs of completion and the estimated costs needed to make the sale.
points.basis: AS 2, definition of net realisable value

points.label: Cost of inventories
points.description: Cost includes all costs of purchase (price, duties and taxes not recoverable, freight inward, less trade discounts and rebates), costs of conversion (direct labour and a systematic allocation of fixed and variable production overheads) and other costs incurred to bring the inventories to their present location and condition.
points.basis: AS 2, cost of inventories: costs of purchase, costs of conversion and other costs

points.label: Costs excluded
points.description: Excluded and charged as expenses: abnormal amounts of wasted materials, labour or other production costs; storage costs unless needed in the production process; administrative overheads that do not help bring inventories to their present location and condition; and selling and distribution costs.
points.basis: AS 2, costs excluded from the cost of inventories

points.label: Cost formulas
points.description: Items not ordinarily interchangeable, or made for specific projects, use specific identification of their costs; other items use the FIFO or weighted average cost formula. Standard cost or the retail method may be used for convenience if the results are close to actual cost.
points.basis: AS 2, cost formulas and techniques for measuring cost
